labeling: W* = executed by candidate in the experiment's isolated python_execute capability (stdlib-only, tiny synthetic data, no host secrets, no network). P* = proposed/UNEXECUTED. An executed witness demonstrates one candidate-authored mechanism in isolation; it does NOT establish full application behavior, engine behavior, or performance on large data.

executed_by_candidate.title: Output-status reducer: stale-on-upstream-edit, unverified-on-kernel-restart
executed_by_candidate.input: In-memory model: 3 notebook cells with stable ids (c1_load, c2_clean, c3_total), one recorded execution event {kernel_epoch, env_hash, per-cell source hashes (sha256), per-dataset content hash}, then (case 1) the load cell is edited and (case 2) the kernel epoch is bumped with nothing else changed.
executed_by_candidate.expected: Case 1: all three outputs stale (edited cell itself plus downstream chain). Case 2: all outputs 'unverified', never 'current'. Precedence: failed > unverified > stale > current.
executed_by_candidate.observed: case1 {c1_load: stale, c2_clean: stale, c3_total: stale}; case2 all 'unverified'; assertions passed; exit 0.
executed_by_candidate.scope_limits: Reducer logic only, on 3 synthetic cells. No real kernel, no real notebook store, no concurrency. The rule set (epoch/env/data/source comparison, document order as dataflow proxy) is a product choice this witness implements, not an external fact.

executed_by_candidate.title: Preview-vs-full type inference mismatch (preview is not full-dataset proof)

prior_failed_run.reason: Candidate-authored expectation was wrong: asserted int(float('1.5')) == 2 (rounding, as DuckDB's scanner reportedly does per issue #25824) but Python's int() truncates to 1. Corrected expectation to 1 with the truncation documented; substantive invariant (silent rewrite under a preview-derived type) unchanged.

executed_by_candidate.input: Synthetic CSV, 104 data rows: 100 rows value '1', then '1.5', '007', '2020-06-15T13:45:59'. Naive per-column type inference over first 10 rows vs full scan; cast of the late value under the preview-derived type.
executed_by_candidate.expected: Preview infers INTEGER, full scan infers VARCHAR; casting late value '1.5' under the preview's assumption silently rewrites it (truncation to 1 in this emulation).
executed_by_candidate.observed: Exactly as expected; assertions passed; exit 0.
executed_by_candidate.scope_limits: Mechanism emulation at toy scale; mirrors the asymmetry documented in duckdb#25824 (S1) but is NOT a DuckDB run and proves nothing about any engine. Real engines differ in cast semantics (DuckDB reportedly rounds; this emulation truncates) — the invariant is 'silently rewritten', not the specific value.

executed_by_candidate.title: Bounded-chunk streaming scan with reject capture and row identity
executed_by_candidate.input: Synthetic 5,442,308-byte CSV (120,000 data rows + header) with one malformed record (5 fields at file line 100,001); processed in fixed 65,536-byte chunks.
executed_by_candidate.expected: Resident bytes bounded by chunk+carry; exactly 1 reject recorded with its line number and byte offset; clean rows + rejects == 120,000 (nothing silently dropped); streaming sha256 computed.
executed_by_candidate.observed: max_bytes_held_at_once 65,579; clean_rows 119,999; malformed_kept_in_rejects 1 at line 100,001 byte_offset 4,516,692; streamed_sha256_prefix 17ae7adb5c116ea0; exit 0.
executed_by_candidate.scope_limits: The synthetic bytes were generated in memory (the generator is not a streaming test); 'bounded' refers to the scan loop. The field check is a naive comma count without CSV quoting. Demonstrates the streaming/reject/row-identity contract shape only; does not demonstrate 5 GB throughput or any real reader.

proposed_unexecuted.title: 5 GB streaming target on the chosen engine
proposed_unexecuted.plan: On an 8-core/16 GB machine, ingest a generated ~5 GB CSV with DuckDB 1.5.x read_csv at defaults, then with explicit columns schema and sample_size=-1; measure peak RSS (must stay well under 16 GB with memory_limit set), wall time, and row-count/hash agreement with a chunked reference reader. Repeat for one aggregation query and one ORDER BY (global op) with temp_directory on local disk.
proposed_unexecuted.expected: Bounded/filter/aggregate operations complete without RSS blowup; a full-file ORDER BY either spills or is refused with an explicit bound message.
proposed_unexecuted.status: UNEXECUTED in this stage: no DuckDB installation or large-data run was possible inside the admitted isolation (no package installation; execution sandbox capped at 256 MB).

proposed_unexecuted.title: Replay determinism of a pinned environment
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Two fresh venvs from a hash-pinned requirements set; run the same 6-cell notebook via nbclient (allow_errors=false, timeout set) on byte-identical synthetic inputs; diff saved outputs cell-by-cell; then perturb one dependency version and confirm outputs are flagged unverified by the env-hash rule.
proposed_unexecuted.expected: Identical outputs under identical pinned env+data; drift detected without execution by env-hash comparison.
proposed_unexecuted.status: UNEXECUTED (no package installation in the admitted sandbox; nbclient not installable here).

proposed_unexecuted.title: Sniffer behavior spot-check on DuckDB 1.5.x
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Reproduce duckdb#25824's minimal CSV (20,479 rows of '1' then '1.5') on installed DuckDB 1.5.x; confirm the silent-rounding behavior and the sample_size=-1 / all_varchar=true recoveries; then run the same file through the wrapper's mandatory explicit-schema path to show the contract prevents it.
proposed_unexecuted.expected: Defaults show 1.5 read back as 2; explicit schema returns the value unchanged.
proposed_unexecuted.status: UNEXECUTED; depends on L2 (issue open, upstream behavior may change).

proposed_unexecuted.title: Crash-recovery of the append-only event journal
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Kill the writer process mid-append (SIGKILL between write and fsync) at 200 randomized offsets; reopen project; assert the journal is either complete to the last committed event or truncated at a record boundary with a recorded partial-tail marker, and that outputs committed before the crash still resolve.
proposed_unexecuted.expected: No torn record ever accepted; no committed output lost.
